title: CI: super run failed on a production candidate
thread:
**Issue #3244 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3244: CI: super run failed on a production candidate
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 42084592622](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42084592622) on #3234, the promotion of `30b65681260f` into production, failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [notebooks](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42084592622/job/127446178471) | failure |
| [e2e component (chrome)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42084592622/job/127457433224) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: production waits on this run, so it is yours and it comes first (`priority:high`). #3234 promotes `30b65681260f`, a commit of `main`, so the fix lands on `main` like any other. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). Say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them. Once the fix is on `main`, the next daily run there that passes promotes it, or a `/promote` on the production issue tests the newer commit sooner.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._
```
